Spoke VPCs /22 each · default route 0.0.0.0/0 to the TGW
Every spoke default route points at the firewall. Prefixes that must NOT be propagated into the spoke table:
on-premises (hybrid domain) and the remote region (peering domain) — either would be more specific than 0.0.0.0/0 and would route around inspection.

GWLBE RT: supernets → TGW, 0.0.0.0/0 → NAT · Public RT: supernets → GWLBE
appliance mode on the inspection attachment
Nothing else. Any propagated prefix here
is more specific than the default and
through the same firewall as a spoke.
On-prem prefixes are propagated OUT of
here into the inspection table, never
default_route_table_association and default_route_table_propagation are both disabled on the TGW. That switches off the implicit
behaviour only — every attachment above is placed in its domain explicitly, which is what makes the routing auditable.
The single rule that holds the whole design together: the spoke table contains exactly one route out, and it points at the firewall.
Every other domain exists so that some prefix — ingress, remote region, on-premises — can be reachable without being propagated into it.
